# Expectation

> Acceptance testing where the behaviour is the source of truth. You write expectations (given/when/then) in a shared vocabulary of states and events; Expectation checks them for conflicts, compiles user stories into acceptance tests, runs them against the system, and writes the user manual with screenshots.

For AI agents: install the skill at https://expectation.sim001.net/skills/expectation/SKILL.md (also /skill.md), or read the whole guide as one text file at https://expectation.sim001.net/llms-full.txt.

## Start here

- [For AI agents](https://expectation.sim001.net/guide/agents.html): commands, workflow and where everything is
- [Skill: expectation](https://expectation.sim001.net/skills/expectation/SKILL.md): the overview skill
- [Skill: write-feature-specs](https://expectation.sim001.net/skills/write-feature-specs/SKILL.md): writing feature specs that make useful docs
- [Getting started](https://expectation.sim001.net/guide/getting-started.html): a complete suite and test in a few minutes
- [The language](https://expectation.sim001.net/guide/language.html): every line of the `.expect` format

## Writing suites

- [Feature docs that explain](https://expectation.sim001.net/guide/feature-docs.html): the depth a feature page needs, with a worked example
- [Writing specs that read well](https://expectation.sim001.net/guide/writing-specs.html)
- [Platforms](https://expectation.sim001.net/guide/platforms.html)
- [From stories to acceptance tests](https://expectation.sim001.net/guide/stories.html)

## Running and publishing

- [Drivers](https://expectation.sim001.net/guide/drivers.html)

- [The expectation command](https://expectation.sim001.net/guide/cli.html)
- [Diagnostics](https://expectation.sim001.net/guide/diagnostics.html)
